A.answer_sk: Nie. Servo, ktoré otočí rukou aspoň o 180° (SCS0009, MG90S ani STS3032), sa do trupu nezmestí. Meral som to na hotovom trupe T4 s krkom a hlavou: mriežka 0,5 mm, otáčanie hlavy ±90,3°, zdvih krku 0–20 mm, vôľa 1,0 mm k pohyblivým a 0,3 mm k pevným dielom. Pri osi ramena je medzi stĺpom a servom zdvihu krku len 1,0 mm. Najväčší voľný kváder pri ramene má 13 × 7,5 × 14 mm a pod bočnými krytmi sú iba štrbiny hlboké 7–8 mm. Telo SCS0009 (aspoň 23,2 × 12,1 × 21,5 mm) som skúšal v 228 natočeniach a nezmestí sa nikde. Najbližšie je ľavý predný roh, kde chýba 1,4 mm, a aj odtiaľ je k osi ramena 40 mm. Servo priamo na osi ramena by z trupu trčalo 9,1 mm a ruka by sa aj tak musela posunúť von o 8,1 mm (v1: 10,5 mm). Navyše by sa musel prerezať stĺp a znova vytlačiť spodok trupu, oba kĺby a oba bočné kryty. Zmestí sa len krídlové servo KST X06, ktoré má rozsah iba 120° a nehlási polohu, a k osi by potrebovalo 40 mm dlhé lanko cez stĺp a objímku krytu. Odporúčam preto ostať pri v1: servo v ruke, ruka posunutá o 10,5–14 mm podľa výšky tela serva a trup bez zmeny.

A.comparison_with_v1:
v1 (servo in the arm, shaft on the axis) needs no torso reprint: the joint takes only a bush and springs. The arm must move out 10.50 mm for a 21.5 mm SCS0009 case and 14.25 mm for a 25.25 mm case (re-checked with the dd2 method, v1_recheck.py). The visible black joint grows from about 4 mm to 15–18 mm, and the base must be about 190 mm wide. v1's weak point: the 3 wires flex across the joint in a half-turn loop on r 11–14, with unverified life (bench test of 10 000 cycles).

Torso direct drive (a) keeps the cable static but still moves the arm out 8.1–11.9 mm, saving only 2.4 mm. It costs a reprint of T_spodok (full torso teardown), 2 × T_klb, 2 × T_bok and new housings. It also cuts the column at shoulder level (stress at least 1.6×, column already over its allowable when alone), and its Ø40 housing is bulkier than v1's joint cover. So it is worse than v1.

No bus servo (SCS0009 / MG90S / STS3032) fits beside or below the column in any orientation; the best miss is 1.4 mm against the exterior walls.

The only torso option that keeps the arm in place (c, KST X06 plus a 40 mm cord) trades a lot away. It has 120° with a 1:1.5 step-up, no feedback and no bus, and it drifts. It also needs new T_klb and T_bok parts, a thinned side-cap wall or a trimmed column head, and it blocks T_stred removal.

Honest balance: v1 has a real but testable risk (wire flex life) and a visible arm shift. Every torso layout either shifts the arm too or gives up range, feedback and robustness, and all of them need several torso parts reprinted. v1 stays the better choice. If the wire flex life fails its test, the fallback is a 3-ring slip contact in the v1 joint, not a torso servo.

Findings the parent should pass on (honest-model issues):
(1) The written proposal leaves a gap in the spring recess. The Ø10.2 recess runs from the column boss face x 38.4 to the step x 44.0 (5.6 mm). A 2 mm flange plus 2 springs (~1.15–1.4 mm) leaves ~2.4 mm, so the model adds a 2.4 mm spacer ring. The alternatives are a 4.4 mm flange or 4 springs.
(2) If the cable chamber is placed axially beside the bearing on the 6.4 mm journal, the plain bearing is only ~3.4 mm long, and the spline also sits at the same x, so the arm would rock. I moved the chamber radially outside a full-length sleeve (journal contact ~6 mm). That makes the black hub r 15.6, larger than the T_klb body r 13.5.
(3) The case sticks out of the white skin by 2.5–8.5 mm, and the cable must leave the chamber at the top for a half-turn wrap. Together these mean the black pod is a sizeable block: from the hub down to ~20 mm below the axis and up to z ≈ -1.4 (the arm top is at +0.9). The visible black joint is ~16 mm long and about 36 mm tall in front view.
(4) The bush must end at x ≤ 57.85 because the servo boss (Ø7 × 1) enters the T_klb bore mouth, so the spline engagement is only ~2.8 mm. With the case at 21.5 the outer-wall margin is 1.6 mm, so dx 12 is just enough; dd2 gives a 14.25 mm shift for a 25.25 case.
(5) The exploded view shows T_klb pulled out for the same reason, an assembly-honesty deviation from the brief.
(6) v1 clearances at head pan 0 / lift 0 / tilt 0: pebble to head ≥ 20.5 mm (at +135), cover to head ≥ 13.7 mm, pebble to torso ≥ 13.3 mm, cover hub to T_bok cap 1.78 mm (constant). A full pan/lift/tilt sweep for v1 was not run.
(7) The servo dimensions, cable exit, screw bosses and the 3 × M2 cover screws are concept-only or unmodelled, as noted on the images.

The user's side question ('nezmestí sa servo do trupu?', can the servo fit in the torso) was not investigated in this step. The images reflect only proposal v1 (servo in the arm).
